verdicts.reason: A puts the tiny three-line body copy at the far left, so it is read before the headline, gives the NEW FLAVOR badge the same weight as the CTA side by side, and shrinks the logo and can to near invisibility. B reads in the right order (headline, then body, then can, then the stacked badge and CTA), but the logo is a speck, the CTA text is tiny and the body copy is very small.

A has the body copy before the headline and a lost logo, but its elements stay in one compact group. B scatters fragments across the banner: a speck of a logo top-left, a NEW FLAVOR badge jammed into the bottom-left that is bigger than the CTA, and a tiny CTA crammed against the top-right edge with unreadable text.

A has the reading-order flaw (body copy before the headline), a badge competing with the CTA, and a near-invisible logo. B centres the headline with its body copy underneath and runs left to right to the can and the CTA, but the NEW FLAVOR badge is jammed into the bottom-left corner, the logo is tiny, and the CTA label is too small to read.
